headline: World Cup rivalry: BNP leader killed in knife attack in Dhaka's Adabor
summary: Abul Bashar Badsha, a local BNP general secretary, died after being attacked with sharp weapons during an arbitration meeting intended to settle a dispute.
details: Abul Bashar Badsha, 30, the general secretary of the Nobodoy Housing unit BNP, was killed after a violent attack with knives and machetes in Dhaka's Adabor on Wednesday night.
The attack occurred around 8:30 PM at Nobodoy Bazar during an arbitration meeting meant to resolve a long-standing dispute at a local shop.
Another leader, Nobodoy Housing unit BNP president Saddam, 35, was also severely injured in the attack, sustaining wounds to his hands, legs, and neck.
Police identified the attackers as Ripon, Nirab, Parvez, and Masum, who are described as members of a local teen gang and followers of a senior BNP vice-president.
Investigation reveals the conflict began on June 29 after a BNP member slapped Ripon during a commotion following a FIFA World Cup match.
The incident led to repeated clashes between the two families, culminating in the fatal attack during the attempt to settle the matter.
Badsha was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital and later transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries at 11:30 PM.
Adabor Police Station Officer-in-Charge Zahidul Islam confirmed the deaths and injuries, stating that efforts are underway to arrest the accused.
caption:
A dispute over a FIFA World Cup match ended in tragedy as a BNP leader was hacked to death in Dhaka.

Abul Bashar Badsha, 30, the general secretary of the Nobodoy Housing unit BNP, was killed after a violent attack with knives and machetes in Dhaka's Adabor on Wednesday night.

The attack occurred around 8:30 PM at Nobodoy Bazar during an arbitration meeting meant to resolve a long-standing dispute at a local shop.

Another leader, Nobodoy Housing unit BNP president Saddam, 35, was also severely injured in the attack, sustaining wounds to his hands, legs, and neck.

Police identified the attackers as Ripon, Nirab, Parvez, and Masum, who are described as members of a local teen gang and followers of a senior BNP vice-president.

Investigation reveals the conflict began on June 29 after a BNP member slapped Ripon during a commotion following a FIFA World Cup match.

The incident led to repeated clashes between the two families, culminating in the fatal attack during the attempt to settle the matter.

Badsha was rushed to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital and later transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries at 11:30 PM.

Adabor Police Station Officer-in-Charge Zahidul Islam confirmed the deaths and injuries, stating that efforts are underway to arrest the accused.

headline_marked: Govt to spend Tk 1,052cr to [[import 2.7 lakh tonnes of wheat]]
headline: Govt to spend Tk 1,052cr to import 2.7 lakh tonnes of wheat
summary: The procurement includes a G2G deal with the US, where wheat will cost $24 per tonne more than the open tender rate to secure trade benefits.
details: The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) has approved the procurement of 2.70 lakh tonnes of wheat. The total cost for the import is Tk 1,052.85 crore, split between a government-to-government (G2G) deal and an international open tender.

Under the G2G arrangement, Bangladesh will import 2.20 lakh tonnes of wheat from the US at a cost of Tk 870 crore, priced at $322 per tonne. This is $24 more per tonne than the open tender rate of $297.92.

The decision aims to comply with US conditions to reduce the bilateral trade deficit, helping Bangladesh secure tariff benefits. This follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed with US Wheat Associates to import up to 700,000 tonnes annually over five years.
Ministry of Food officials noted that the quality of US wheat has exceeded expectations, with a protein content of 13.5 percent, surpassing the contracted minimum of 11.5 percent.
Beyond wheat, the CCGP also approved the import of two LNG cargoes costing Tk 1,438 crore and 75,000 tonnes of MOP fertiliser from Russia and Canada costing Tk 351 crore.
Additionally, the government cleared two road upgrade projects connecting Lakshmipur, Noakhali, and Feni districts with the National Special Economic Zone at a total cost of Tk 281 crore.

The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) has approved the procurement of 2.70 lakh tonnes of wheat. The total cost for the import is Tk 1,052.85 crore, split between a government-to-government (G2G) deal and an international open tender.

Under the G2G arrangement, Bangladesh will import 2.20 lakh tonnes of wheat from the US at a cost of Tk 870 crore, priced at $322 per tonne. This is $24 more per tonne than the open tender rate of $297.92.

The decision aims to comply with US conditions to reduce the bilateral trade deficit, helping Bangladesh secure tariff benefits. This follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed with US Wheat Associates to import up to 700,000 tonnes annually over five years.

Ministry of Food officials noted that the quality of US wheat has exceeded expectations, with a protein content of 13.5 percent, surpassing the contracted minimum of 11.5 percent.

Beyond wheat, the CCGP also approved the import of two LNG cargoes costing Tk 1,438 crore and 75,000 tonnes of MOP fertiliser from Russia and Canada costing Tk 351 crore.

Additionally, the government cleared two road upgrade projects connecting Lakshmipur, Noakhali, and Feni districts with the National Special Economic Zone at a total cost of Tk 281 crore.
